text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: The records office filed routine paperwork by logging each transaction against a dated field, linking the entry to a named account, and retaining a sign-off token; unverified fields remained open for audit without automatic closure, and each document carried a single identifying value per action.

2) What occurred: The actor created a first document containing a valid ticket identifier; the authenticity check on that document remained unverified. The actor created a second document reusing the same ticket identifier; the duplicate-detection check on that document remained unverified. The actor created a third document reusing the same ticket identifier; the duplicate-detection check on that document remained unverified. The actor transmitted the first document to a buyer channel; the buyer-identity field on that transmission remained unverified. The actor transmitted the second document to a buyer channel; the buyer-identity field on that transmission remained unverified. The actor transmitted the third document to a buyer channel; the buyer-identity field on that transmission remained unverified. The actor applied a modification to the first document's entry sequence; the sequence-order check on that modification remained unverified. The actor removed a refund-request field from the first document; the refund-status check on that removal remained unverified. The actor removed a chargeback-flag field from the first document; the chargeback-status check on that removal remained unverified. The actor replaced the actor-identification field with an obfuscated value; the identification check on that replacement remained unverified.

3) Materials/access observed: One valid ticket identifier. Three documents each containing that identifier. A buyer channel. A modification tool applied to entry-sequence fields. Two removal operations on refund and chargeback fields. An obfuscated value applied to the identification field. Access to a named account.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Duplicate ticket identifiers across distinct document fields. Unverified authenticity and duplicate-detection checks. Unverified buyer-identity fields across transmissions. Modified entry-sequence values. Removed refund and chargeback status fields. Obfuscated identification value. Dated records without sign-off tokens.
